answers.1_provider_chain_construction: llm.py lines 46-67 define CHAINS dict; 'chat'/'ollama' chains = [kimi_k2_6_cloud, codex, llama8b, deepseek14b]
answers.2_why_chain_order_changed: llm.py lines 356-386: pre-flight ctx routing reorders chain when _force_reorder=true. _force_reorder comes from _chain_in_cooldown(model_priority) which triggers when chain failure rate > 5% over last 100 queries. During reorder, non-ollama providers (codex) are placed before ollama providers (kimi_k2_6_cloud).
answers.3_chain_order_affected_by_prior_failures: Yes. _chain_in_cooldown() checks _GLOBAL_CHAIN_HEALTH deque of last 100 outcomes. If failure_rate > 0.05, chain enters 600s cooldown and reorder is forced.
answers.4_kimi_moved_to_end_after_timeout: Yes. Because MODELS['kimi_k2_6_cloud']['type'] = 'ollama' and MODELS['codex']['type'] = 'codex_cli'. Reorder sorts non-ollama first, then ollama by ctx size. This puts codex at position 0 and kimi at the end.
answers.5_budget_shared_across_providers: Yes. max_time is passed to llm.query() from session.py (BRAIN_CHAT_LLM_TIMEOUT=90). Budget is consumed cumulatively across all providers in the chain.
answers.6_per_provider_timeout: Yes. MODELS defines per-provider timeout: kimi_k2_6_cloud=75, codex=120, llama8b=60, deepseek14b=90.
answers.7_same_provider_retry: No. The loop iterates each provider once. There is no retry logic for the same provider.
answers.8_fallback_after_kimi_timeout: Fallback happens by advancing to next provider in chain. But if chain is reordered, codex is tried first, not kimi. If codex times out, budget is exhausted before reaching kimi.
answers.9_why_fallback_says_kimi_skipped_by_budg: In probes 2/3, chain was [codex, llama8b, deepseek14b, kimi]. Codex attempted first and used budget. By the time the loop reached kimi, remaining budget < 8s (min_provider_budget), so kimi was skipped with 'budget exhausted'.
answers.10_can_llm_grounded_cycle_force_kimi_fir: Currently NO. llm.py does not receive metadata flags (read_only, evaluation, llm_grounded_cycle). The chain reorder happens purely based on _chain_in_cooldown() and estimated input tokens. However, a patch can: (a) preserve kimi_k2_6_cloud at position 0 during reorder, or (b) pass metadata to llm.query() to suppress reorder for safe eval routes.
